paths.description: Homepage and first-load consent state; represents entry, search, category discovery, preferences, privacy, performance, and mobile adaptation.
Handy & Telefon category results; represents search/listing cards, filters, result semantics, repeated scrolling, mobile adaptation, and memory behaviour.
Live classified detail; represents product metadata, price, seller/message CTA, recommendations, and rich-entity discoverability.
Guest primary journey from discovery through category results to a live classified detail.
Authentication entry and invalid-email recovery; also represents the account wall reached from posting.
Deliberate invalid route; represents HTTP failure and recovery.

findings.summary: The public marketplace is fixed to a light palette even when the user requests dark mode.
findings.evidence: Computed-style probes under light and dark both returned color-scheme: normal, body background rgb(255,255,255), and dialog background rgb(247,247,247); the dark-condition screenshot remains light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and map surface, text, border, focus, and overlay tokens through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), including the consent dialog.

findings.summary: The listing keeps the same non-essential three-second animation when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The normal and prefers-reduced-motion: reduce probes each found a finished animation with duration 3000ms; the reduced condition did not shorten or remove it.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential transitions and animations in a no-preference query and provide an instant or substantially reduced alternative under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: Navigation between the home, results, and detail templates swaps abruptly without View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition declarations while the tested primary journey crosses full documents between three distinct templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin browse navigation, with restrained shared-element treatment and a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures the primary marketplace content on every fresh visit, especially on mobile.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360px screenshots show an open modal covering most or all of the initial viewport before interaction; on mobile the long consent copy occupies the whole left panel and dims the marketplace.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the full-screen first-load interruption with a compact, content-preserving consent surface that keeps accept and reject actions immediately available and accessible.

findings.summary: The templates adapt at the viewport level but expose no container-query strategy for reusable cards and filters.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found responsive mobile layouts but no @container or container-type declarations, while listing cards are reused across home, results, and recommendations at different widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card/filter shells containment and move component-specific breakpoints to @container rules, retaining viewport queries only for page-level composition.

findings.summary: Lab performance is poor on both home and listing templates.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured home LCP 12.1s, CLS 1.0, TBT 210ms and performance 37; listing LCP 12.4s, CLS 1.011, TBT 250ms and performance 34. The independent trace measured LCP 5.14s.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency chain, prioritize the actual LCP resource, reserve overlay/content space, and defer non-critical experiments, ads, and analytics until after the primary content is usable.

findings.summary: Large layout shifts occur during cold load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported CLS 1.0 on home and 1.011 on listing. The isolated layout observer started after page setup and saw zero, so the Lighthouse cold-load result captures shifts missed by the late observer.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify the cold-load shift sources, reserve dimensions for consent/ad/media slots, and avoid replacing initial layout geometry after first paint.

findings.summary: Advertising, analytics, experimentation, and legacy bundles dominate the initial load.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 148 requests and 1.83MB transferred, including 67 scripts and 1.46MB script bytes. Lighthouse estimated 524–584KiB unused JavaScript and 73–75KiB unused CSS; the HAR identifies GTM/gtag/prebid and experimentation among the largest resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a first-load script budget, remove duplicate/legacy bundles, gate ads and experiments behind consent and relevance, and lazy-load route-specific code after primary content.

findings.summary: Critical accessible-name and ARIA defects appear on results, detail, and login templates.
findings.evidence: axe found invalid ARIA values on both search fields and an unnamed sorting button on results; detail repeats invalid ARIA; login has one image without alt and two links without discernible names.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the invalid ARIA attribute values, give icon-only sort/back/logo controls explicit names, and provide meaningful logo alt text or mark decorative imagery appropriately.

findings.summary: The listing template exposes an incoherent heading hierarchy and the detail contains invalid list/landmark structure.
findings.evidence: The listing probe found eleven H1 elements, including advertising product names as well as the actual results heading. axe found a detail-page li outside a list and a complementary landmark nested inside another landmark.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep one page H1, demote card/ad titles to appropriate lower headings, contain every li in a list, and make complementary landmarks top-level where required.

findings.summary: Listing and home images frequently omit intrinsic dimensions and below-fold loading is too eager.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 29 of 30 listing images without width/height and 26 below-fold images not lazy; home had 37 of 42 without dimensions, 34 without srcset, and 25 without alt. Lighthouse separately identified unsized advertiser logos on listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or aspect-ratio for every image, lazy-load below-fold results, and provide responsive srcset/sizes and meaningful alt where images convey content.

findings.summary: The site disables BFCache and ships missing or broken source maps for large scripts.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three BFCache failure reasons led by Cache-Control: no-store and multiple missing, forbidden, or malformed source maps for large first-party and analytics scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid no-store on cache-safe public documents and publish valid production source maps with correct access controls.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP is absent and several cookies are not Secure.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no Content-Security-Policy. Cookie inspection found five flagged cookies, including insecure kameleoonVisitorCode and bm_sz cookies with SameSite=None; one duplicate visitor cookie lasts 380 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, set Secure on all HTTPS cookies, tighten SameSite, deduplicate the visitor cookie, and shorten non-essential retention.

findings.summary: The first-load privacy footprint is large before the user has made a consent choice.
findings.evidence: The consent dialog names 301 partners. The HAR recorded 72 cross-origin requests and 725KB classified cross-origin; tracker inspection saw Google Tag Manager and Google syndication plus Kameleoon, while the modal was still open.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to a minimal, no-personalization request set before consent; delay tag managers, ad auctions, and experimentation until an informed opt-in and continuously reduce vendor count.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are missing.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Clickjacking protection, HSTS, and nosniff were present, so this is a partial policy gap rather than absent transport defense.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; express frame protection in CSP frame-ancestors when CSP is deployed.

findings.summary: The consent design strongly privileges acceptance and makes refusal comparatively hard to find.
findings.evidence: The modal presents a large bright “Alle akzeptieren” button while rejection appears only as a small inline “ablehnen, ändern oder widerrufen” link below settings; mobile preserves this unequal hierarchy while blocking content.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer equally prominent Accept and Reject actions in the first layer, use neutral visual weighting, and keep granular settings optional rather than the path to refusal.

taskList.title: Redesign consent to preserve content, offer equal reject, and suppress non-essential vendors before opt-in
Cut initial script/advertising cost and repair LCP/CLS on home and listing
Fix critical ARIA, control names, heading, list, and landmark semantics
Deploy CSP and complete cookie and browser-policy hardening
Add intrinsic image sizing, responsive sources, alt text, and below-fold lazy loading
Adopt component queries and restrained cross-document transitions
Restore BFCache eligibility and valid source maps
